messages.content: Describe the difference between Lagrangian and Eulerian methods.

The Lagrangian and Eulerian methods are two ways to describe fluid motion. In the Lagrangian method, the motion of individual fluid particles is tracked to observe changes in their properties. It is also known as a material description because it follows a material (fluid) particle. In contrast, the Eulerian method tracks the fluid properties at a fixed point in space. It is also known as a field description because it concerns fields, i.e., properties like velocity, pressure and temperature that vary in time and space. Given an object representing a 3D mesh that is made of of faces containing both quads and tris. What would be the best term to use when referring to both the quads and tris together?
The term commonly used to refer to both quads and tris in a 3D mesh is "polygons". So, you can say that the mesh is made up of polygons, where some of the polygons are quads and others are tris.
